label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
# Helping your midwife find you

**From your Riverside community midwives**

Hello! My manager Deb asked me to write this page because I am the midwife on our team who always gets lost. It is true. I have driven round the same block of flats for 20 minutes. I have followed my sat nav to a chippy. I once walked into the wrong house because the door was open, and a very nice old man gave me a Jammie Dodger anyway.

So please read this page. When it is 3am and your baby is coming, we want to be inside your house, not outside looking for it.

In the Philippines, where I am from, we say the midwife is like family. That is how we want to arrive at your door: like a friend who already knows the way.

## First, the dates

Home birth cover starts from **37 weeks** of pregnancy. If labour starts before 37 weeks, you go to the hospital instead.

We tell everybody this at the booking visit and everybody forgets, so here it is again in writing.

## How to call us

1. When labour starts, phone the **Riverside birth line: [NUMBER]**.
2. Please do not phone or text a midwife's personal mobile, even if you have mine. I might be asleep, off duty, or on a beach. The birth line goes to whoever is on call.
3. Say your name and your full address. Tell us anything that helps us find you, like "the blue door next to the bus stop".
4. Send your location to the birth line phone. There are two easy ways:
   - **WhatsApp:** send us a location pin.
   - **what3words:** this is a free app that gives every small square of the world its own three words. Open the app at your front door and send us your three words. I did not believe in it at first, but it is good, actually.

## Help us find the right door

**Show your house number.** Make sure we can see it from the road, in the dark, in the rain. I once looked for a house that had no number, only a name, "Rosemary Cottage", in a long street of terraces. That was the night my sat nav took me to the chippy. If your house has a name and no number, tell us what is next door.

**If you live in a flat, give us the full directions.** Tell us which building, which entrance and which floor. In one block in Everton, flat 14 was not next to flat 13. It was in a different building. In the end the dad waved a tea towel from the window and I found them.

**Put the porch light on.** At night in winter, all the dark streets look the same. If you have an outside light, please switch it on when you call us.

**Give us a sign.** One family tied balloons on the gate, like for a party. Best idea ever. I found the house straight away. A tea towel in the window works too, as you now know.

**Send someone to the door.** If there is another adult in the house, ask them to watch for us and wave.

## Parking

Two midwives come to your birth, and we usually come in separate cars. So if it is possible, we need **two parking spaces**, as near to your door as you can manage.

This is not because we are lazy. We carry a lot: the gas and air cylinders, the big bag, and sometimes things for the birthing pool. By the time we reach your door, our arms are already tired, and we need them for you.

**If you live in a permit zone** (there are lots around Anfield and Kensington), please ask the council about a visitor permit before your due date. Keep it by the front door so we can put it on the dashboard as soon as we arrive. We have had parking tickets before while delivering babies. The baby was worth it, but still.

## Inside the house

**Pets in another room, please.** I love dogs. There is a staffie called Pippin who loves me too much. Pippin jumped on me at every visit, and one time I nearly dropped the gas and air. So I love dogs, but not during the pushing. Before we arrive, please put your pets in another room with the door shut.

**Clear the hallway and the stairs.** We will be carrying heavy things and we cannot always see our feet. Please move the shoes, the washing basket and the Lego. Especially the Lego.

## That is all

None of this is to tell you off. Every home is different and we are happy to come to all of them. We only want to get to you fast, with all our equipment and no parking ticket.

See you soon. I will try to arrive at the right house.

**[YOUR NAME]**
Riverside community midwives

## Fridge checklist

Cut this out or take a photo, and stick it on the fridge.

**Get ready before 37 weeks**

☐ We know home birth cover starts from 37 weeks (before that, we go to the hospital)

☐ The birth line number is saved in our phones: [NUMBER]

☐ We know how to send a WhatsApp pin or our what3words

☐ Our house number is easy to see from the road

☐ If we live in a flat: we have written down the building, entrance and floor

☐ The porch light works

☐ If we are in a permit zone: the visitor permit is by the front door

☐ We have a plan for the pets

**When labour starts**

☐ Phone the birth line (not a midwife's personal mobile)

☐ Send our location to the birth line phone

☐ Porch light on

☐ Two parking spaces free, if possible

☐ Pets in another room, door shut

☐ Hallway and stairs clear (shoes, washing basket, Lego)

☐ Balloons on the gate (not needed, but brilliant)

Before this goes out:

- **Placeholders:** the birth line number goes in twice, and your name goes at the bottom.
- **Hospital number:** you might want to add it under "First, the dates", since I didn't have it.
- **Names:** Pippin and Rosemary Cottage could be recognised in the Facebook group, so check those families don't mind, or change the names.
